name: Sandisk
description: Sandisk designs and sells NAND flash storage: enterprise SSDs for data centers, SSDs and embedded flash for phones, PCs, cars and consoles (Edge), and retail cards, USB drives and portable SSDs under the Sandisk brand (Consumer). It makes its flash in joint ventures with Kioxia in Japan (Flash Ventures), buying about half the output at cost. Revenue rose 175 percent to $20.2B in fiscal 2026 on higher prices and Datacenter demand, and operating margin went from negative to 61 percent. It is moving to multi-year "New Business Model" supply contracts with customer cash advances and guarantees: two more with $31.3B of transaction price were signed after year end.

businessLines.name: Edge
businessLines.how: Flash storage sold per unit (by capacity) to device makers and channel partners; revenue is gigabytes shipped times price per gigabyte, which rose sharply in FY2026.
businessLines.description: SSDs for PCs, gaming consoles and set-top boxes; embedded flash for phones, tablets, cars, IoT, industrial and connected home, sold to OEM and channel customers.

businessLines.name: Datacenter
businessLines.how: Enterprise SSDs sold per unit under increasingly long-term contracts; the new agreements commit customers to specified volumes over multiple years with financial guarantees and advance payments.
businessLines.description: Enterprise SSDs for cloud service providers, private cloud and enterprise servers, including AI workloads.

businessLines.name: Consumer
businessLines.how: Branded products sold per unit through retailers and distributors; revenue fell in volume and rose on price in FY2026.
businessLines.description: Retail SSDs, memory cards, USB flash drives and portable storage under the Sandisk brand, through retail and channel.

brands.segment: Some products sold under licence from WDC for a limited transitional period
